_comment: P-TQA.7 — accepted/pre-existing high+critical advisories. The audit gate (scripts/auditGate.mjs) BLOCKS any high/critical NOT listed here. Each entry is triaged: dev-only, no safe fix, or a separate upgrade task. Re-triage periodically and remove once fixed. A NEW high/critical in any other package fails CI.

allow.reason: dev-only test runner (not shipped to users); fix requires a major-version bump tracked as a separate task.
dev-only coverage tool (P-TQA.1); same advisory as vitest (via: vitest) — fix is a semver-major vitest 4 upgrade tracked with the vitest entry. Never shipped to users.
dev/build-only toolchain (not shipped at runtime); upgrade tracked separately to avoid a risky major bump.
pre-existing transitive; upgrade evaluated separately (used server-side; needs regression check before bumping).
payments SDK; vendor-pinned — upgrade requires payment-flow re-verification, tracked separately.
transitive dependency; no direct fix without upstream bump — tracked separately.
transitive dependency; pre-existing, upgrade tracked separately.
no upstream fix available on npm (prototype-pollution/ReDoS advisories); usage is server-side and input-controlled — tracked separately.

freshly-published DoS-only advisory (exponential-time {} expansion) in a deep transitive dep (via glob/minimatch, build/dev tooling). Patched versions are split across majors (1.x/2.x/5.x) whose consumers need different APIs, so a global override risks breaking consumers; `npm audit fix` restructures the whole lockfile (~3k-line churn) = real breakage risk. Not user-runtime, DoS-only — accepted; proper dedupe/upgrade tracked separately.

freshly-published DoS-only advisory (quadratic CPU via YAML merge-key alias chains) in a transitive dev/build dep. Installed across majors 3.x/4.x whose APIs differ (a forced 5.x override would break 3.x consumers); no safe surgical fix without a lockfile-wide restructure. DoS-only, not user-runtime input — accepted; upgrade tracked separately.

freshly-published DoS/crash-only advisories (PAX path type confusion, unbounded decompression) in a transitive build/tooling dep (not on any user-facing request path). A clean tar@7.5.16→7.5.20 patch exists, but applying it regenerates/dedupes the whole lockfile (~3k-line churn) = breakage risk against the never-break rule; deferred to a dedicated, verified dependency-bump PR. DoS-only — accepted meanwhile.
